title: Restriction preserves the lower-support component
statement: Let $\Omega$ and $\iota$ be finite nonempty sets, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, and let $B$ be a basis of real-valued functions on $\Omega$ whose constant-one element is indexed by $0$ and which is orthonormal for the $\pi$-weighted inner product. For a positive integer $n$, a function $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$, a set $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, a coordinate $i\in S$, and a state $\omega\in\Omega$, applying the orthogonal-component projection for $S\setminus\{i\}$ to the function obtained by fixing coordinate $i$ of the orthogonal component for $S$ at $\omega$ leaves that function unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: Finite nonempty basis index set $\iota$ with decidable equality
A basis element indexed by $0$ is constant one
The basis is orthonormal for the $\pi$-weighted inner product
